claims.text: Catalytic activity in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts is governed by formation of a specific Pt-Pd-Rh surface ensemble.
The Pt-Pd-Rh surface ensemble enhances ethanol adsorption and dissociation.
Enhanced ethanol adsorption and dissociation improves catalytic performance.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a uniform distribution of elements.
Controlled addition of Rh to the catalyst surface produces the stated Pt0.4Pd0.3Rh0.2Ru0.05Ir0.05Os0.05 surface composition.
The relevant mediator after the intervention is a Pt-Pd-Rh surface ensemble.
At 300°C, 1 atm, 1 M ethanol, and 10 mL/min flow, the modified catalyst will exhibit enhanced ethanol adsorption and dissociation.
The modified catalyst will show a 25% increase in ethanol-to-CO2 conversion rate relative to the stated baseline.
The comparison baseline has surface composition Pt0.5Pd0.3Ru0.1Ir0.05Os0.05.
The proposed mechanism holds from 250–350°C, 0.5–1.5 atm, and 0.5–2 M ethanol.
The magnitude of the activity increase may depend on experimental conditions and the accuracy of surface-composition control.
An activity increase below 10% relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated modified composition Pt0.4Pd0.3Rh0.2Ru0.05Ir0.05Os0.05 sums to 1.05 rather than 1.00, so it is not a valid normalized surface composition as written.
The material and baseline are labeled PtPdRhRuIrOs, but the stated baseline composition contains no Rh.
The intervention is described only as introduction of Rh, but the stated change also lowers Pt from 0.50 to 0.40 and Ru from 0.10 to 0.05 while producing a non-normalized total.
